name: Methyl lactate
description: Methyl lactate (CAS 547-64-8 ) is the methyl ester of lactic acid, functioning as a biodegradable solvent and pH modifier across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial processing applications. Derived from renewable feedstocks, it offers a greener alternative to conventional polar solvents in formulations and manufacturing processes. In electronics, it is used as a photoresist stripper. It effectively removes residues from circuit boards without the toxicity profile of chlorinated alternatives. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a solvent and mild acidulant in skin-conditioning products. Its compatibility with aqueous and organic phases supports stable emulsion systems. In printing and packaging, it functions as a solvent carrier in ink formulations, improving flow and substrate adhesion. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a process solvent in active ingredient synthesis and as a carrier in topical preparations requiring controlled pH. It is supplied as a clear liquid. Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial solvent applications and high-purity grades meeting pharmaceutical and food-grade specifications such as USP and FCC standards. Buyers should confirm optical purity requirements, as both racemic (DL) and enantiomerically enriched forms are available depending on the application.
